description: MAP-E CE dashboard combining mape-prometheus-metrics health checks, PF queue metrics, node_exporter textfile freshness, and pfctl_exporter-compatible metrics. Rate queries use the $rate_window variable instead of Grafana $__rate_interval because the textfile collector is commonly refreshed once per minute.

panels.description: Boolean health checks emitted by mape-prometheus-metrics. maped_up and dhcp6leased_up come from rcctl; dhcp6leased_mape_bound confirms the DHCPv6 MAP-E option is present; pppoe_session_up checks WAN link state; mape_gif_up and mape_gif_running check the gif tunnel; mape_anchor_portset_present and mape_anchor_file_portset_present verify live and generated PF map-e-portset rules; mape_default_route_v4/v6 check expected routing; mape_derive_ok confirms maped-derive can calculate CE IPv6 and MAP-E IPv4 values.
panels.title: MAP-E Health

panels.description: Age in seconds of /var/prometheus/textfile/mape.prom as observed by node_exporter. This should stay close to the cron interval; sustained age above a few minutes means the collector is stale even if Prometheus can still scrape node_exporter.
panels.title: Textfile Freshness

panels.description: node_textfile_scrape_error is 1 when node_exporter cannot read one or more textfile collector files. Keep this at 0 before trusting the MAP-E and PF metrics.
panels.title: Textfile Scrape Error

panels.description: Traffic rate through PF queues reported by pfctl -sq -v. pf_queue_bytes_total is cumulative bytes per queue; rate over $rate_window converts it to bytes/sec and the panel multiplies by 8 for bits/sec.
panels.title: MAP-E Queue Throughput

panels.description: Current PF queue occupancy as a percentage of configured queue limit. pf_queue_length and pf_queue_limit are gauges from pfctl -sq -v; sustained non-zero fill suggests congestion.
panels.title: MAP-E Queue Fill

panels.description: Drop rate per PF queue. pf_queue_dropped_packets_total is cumulative dropped packets per queue; non-zero rates on mape_std usually mean the queue is saturated or mis-sized.
panels.title: MAP-E Queue Drops
Total Rule Evaluations / sec
panels.description: Total rate at which PF rules are evaluated. pfctl_rule_evaluations_total is a cumulative per-rule counter; rate over $rate_window makes it evaluations/sec and sum by instance gives router-wide rule evaluation pressure.

panels.title: Top ${top} Rules by Evaluations / sec
panels.description: Highest-rate PF rules by evaluation count. This helps find rules that dominate packet-filter work; it uses pfctl_rule_evaluations_total over $rate_window.

panels.title: Rule Evaluations
panels.description: Rule evaluation rate panels. These use $rate_window so the PromQL range is safely longer than the mape-prometheus-metrics textfile refresh cadence.

panels.title: Top${top} Rules by Traffic (bits/sec)
panels.description: Highest-throughput PF rules by bytes matched. pfctl_rule_bytes_total is cumulative bytes; rate over $rate_window multiplied by 8 gives bits/sec.

panels.title: Top${top} Rules by traffic (packets/sec)
panels.description: Highest packet-rate PF rules. pfctl_rule_packets_total is cumulative packets; rate over $rate_window gives packets/sec.

panels.title: Top${top} Rules by average packet size in bytes
panels.description: Approximate average packet size per rule, calculated as byte rate divided by packet rate over $rate_window. Very low packet rates can make this noisy.

panels.title: Top${top} Rules by State Creations / sec
panels.description: Highest state-creation rules. pfctl_rule_states_total is exported as a cumulative rule state counter by pfctl_exporter; rate over $rate_window smooths textfile collection cadence.

panels.title: Top Rules by Traffic and State Creation
panels.description: Top-k rule panels for bytes, packets, average packet size, and state creation counters.

panels.title: Total State Creations / sec
panels.description: Total PF state creation rate by instance from pfctl_rule_states_total. This is a rate panel, so it uses the dashboard $rate_window instead of Grafana $__rate_interval to avoid windows shorter than the textfile refresh interval.

panels.title: State Creations
panels.description: State creation rate panels. The dashboard uses $rate_window instead of Grafana $__rate_interval to avoid sparse textfile samples.

panels.title: pf firewall states
panels.description: Current PF state table entries from pfctl_state_table_current_entries. This is a gauge, so it should not be wrapped in rate().

panels.title: pf firewall states
panels.description: Current PF state table entries from pfctl_state_table_current_entries. This is a gauge, so it should not be wrapped in rate().

panels.title: State Table Searches / sec
panels.description: PF state table lookup rate from pfctl_state_table_searches_total. This is useful for broad firewall workload trends.

panels.title: State Table Inserts / sec
panels.description: PF state table insertion rate from pfctl_state_table_inserts_total. This is often a better global view of new connection/state churn than per-rule topk panels.

panels.title: State Table Removals / sec
panels.description: PF state table removal rate from pfctl_state_table_removals_total. Compare with inserts/sec and current entries to spot churn or expiry behavior.

panels.title: State Table
panels.description: Current PF state table size and global state-table operation counters.

Instant traffic split by address family for the selected action. pfctl_interface_bytes_total is cumulative bytes by interface, direction, family, and PF action; rate over $rate_window converts it to traffic rate.
panels.title: ${action}ed traffic by family

targets.expr: sum(rate(pfctl_interface_bytes_total{instance=~"$instance", interface=~"$interface", action="${action}", direction="In", family=~"$family"}[$rate_window])) by (family, instance) * 8 > 0
sum(rate(pfctl_interface_bytes_total{instance=~"$instance", interface=~"$interface", action="${action}", direction="Out", family=~"$family"}[$rate_window])) by (family, instance) * -8 < 0

panels.title: ${action}ed traffic by family (In + / Out -)
panels.description: Traffic over time split by IPv4/IPv6, with inbound positive and outbound negative. This makes direction changes visible without separate panels.

panels.title: ${action}ed traffic by interface
panels.description: Instant traffic split by interface for the selected PF action and filters.

targets.expr: sum(rate(pfctl_interface_bytes_total{instance=~"$instance", interface=~"$interface", action="${action}", direction="In", family=~"$family"}[$rate_window])) by (interface, instance) * 8 > 0
sum(rate(pfctl_interface_bytes_total{instance=~"$instance", interface=~"$interface", action="${action}", direction="Out", family=~"$family"}[$rate_window])) by (interface, instance) * -8 < 0

panels.title: ${action}ed traffic by interface (In + / Out -)
panels.description: Traffic over time split by interface, with inbound positive and outbound negative.

panels.title: ${action}ed traffic by direction
panels.description: Instant traffic split by PF direction for the selected action and filters.

targets.expr: sum(rate(pfctl_interface_bytes_total{instance=~"$instance", interface=~"$interface", action="${action}", direction="In", family=~"$family"}[$rate_window])) by (direction, instance) * 8
sum(rate(pfctl_interface_bytes_total{instance=~"$instance", interface=~"$interface", action="${action}", direction="Out", family=~"$family"}[$rate_window])) by (direction, instance) * -8

panels.title: ${action}ed traffic by direction (in + / out -)
panels.description: Traffic over time by direction, with inbound positive and outbound negative.

panels.title: ${action}ed traffic by interface, family (in + / out -)
panels.description: Detailed traffic series by interface and address family, with inbound positive and outbound negative.

panels.title: ${action}ed Traffic
panels.description: Interface traffic counters split by PF action, direction, interface, and address family.

targets.expr: sum(rate(pfctl_table_bytes_total{instance=~"$instance", action=~"$action", direction="In", table=~"$table"}[$rate_window])) by (table, action, direction, instance) * 8
sum(rate(pfctl_table_bytes_total{instance=~"$instance", action=~"$action", direction="Out", table=~"$table"}[$rate_window])) by (table, action, direction, instance) * -8

panels.title: Traffic Details for Table $table (In + / Out -)
panels.description: Traffic rate for selected PF tables. pfctl_table_bytes_total is cumulative table traffic by action and direction; rate over $rate_window converts it to bits/sec, with outbound shown negative.

panels.title: Table Traffic Details
panels.description: PF table traffic counters and rates for selected tables.

panels.title: Table Addresses
panels.description: Current number of addresses in each selected PF table from pfctl_table_addresses. This is a gauge and should not be rated.

panels.title: Table Addresses
panels.description: Current number of addresses in each selected PF table from pfctl_table_addresses. This is a gauge and should not be rated.

panels.title: $counter / sec
panels.description: Selected PF global counter rate from the pfctl_counters_*_total metric family. Use this to inspect drops/errors such as state_mismatch, short, no_route, or ip_option.

panels.title: Counters
panels.description: PF global counter rates from pfctl -vvs info.

panels.title: $limit_counter / sec
panels.description: Selected PF limit counter rate from the pfctl_limit_counters_*_total metric family. These counters indicate PF limits being reached.

panels.title: Limit Counters
panels.description: PF limit counter rates from pfctl -vvs info.

list.description: PF queue names exported by mape-prometheus-metrics from pfctl -sq -v, such as mape_std and mape_voip.
list.name: queue

list.description: Custom filters (will be applied to all panels)
list.name: filter

list.description: PromQL range for rate() queries. Keep this several times larger than the mape-prometheus-metrics textfile refresh interval; 5m works well for a 60s cron job.
list.name: rate_window

list.description: How many entries to include in the "topk" panels
list.name: top
